channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Healthcare Funding to Nearly Triple by 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's healthcare sector funding is projected to increase nearly threefold, from 26 billion soms in 2021 to 73.1 billion soms by 2026. This significant boost, part of ongoing economic reforms, will support modernization of medical infrastructure, equipment upgrades, and improved working conditions for medical staff. The government also handed over 73 new ambulances.

item.title: Tajikistan Reports Significant Growth in Freight and Passenger Transport
item.description: From January to September 2026, Tajikistan saw a 15.6% increase in freight transport and a 9.9% rise in passenger transport compared to the same period last year. Road transport accounted for the majority of freight, carrying 127 million tons, a 16% increase. Rail transport moved 5.94 million tons, up 6.4%.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Average Salary Jumps 12-Fold Over Two Decades Amidst Economic Growth
item.description: The average salary in Kazakhstan has increased nearly 12 times, from 40,800 tenge in 2006 to 486,400 tenge in Q2 2026. Average monthly expenses per person rose approximately 9.5 times during the same period. Nominal GDP grew significantly, contributing to increased household incomes and expenditures, though unevenly across different goods.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank Adjusts Gold Bar Prices, TROY Ounce Sees Notable Increase
item.description: The National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic raised selling prices for 10, 31.1035, and 100-gram gold bars by 0.51-0.52% on November 16. Prices for 1, 2, and 5-gram bars remained unchanged. Buy-back prices for all six types of gold bars increased by 0.46-0.52%. The selling price of a troy ounce rose by 1,780 soms to 347,695 soms.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Regulate Children's Online Games with New Bill
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing a new bill, "On Digital and Information Security of Children," to enhance child safety in online environments. The proposed measures include requirements for platforms to label digital risks like in-game purchases and chat features. An official verification mechanism and monitoring for violations are also planned.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Reports Rise in Public Inflation Expectations
item.description: Public inflation expectations in Uzbekistan have increased for the first time since March, according to the Central Bank's October survey. The average forecast for price growth in the next 12 months rose to 9.1%. Tashkent, Jizzakh, and Fergana showed the highest expectations, while energy and utility costs remain key influencing factors.

item.title: Two Candidates Collect Required Signatures for Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: Two candidates have gathered the necessary signatures to run in the upcoming presidential election in Kyrgyzstan. President Sadyr Japarov has collected over 60,000 signatures, while Siyymyk Japykeev has over 31,000. The signature collection process continues until December 8, with the election scheduled for January 27, 2027.

item.title: Marat Irmenov Appointed Chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee
item.description: Marat Irmenov has been appointed as the new chairman of the National Security Committee (KNB) of Kazakhstan by presidential decree. He was previously serving as deputy chairman. Irmenov has a background in security services and holds a general-major rank.

item.title: Thousands Protest in Prague Against Government Media Law Changes
item.description: Up to 450,000 people demonstrated in Prague to support independent media and protest against the government's planned changes to the financing of Czech Television and Radio. Protesters expressed concern over the rushed adoption of important laws without public discussion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Chairman of National Security Committee
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Marat Gataullyuly Irmenov as the new Chairman of the National Security Committee. Irmenov was previously dismissed from his prior position. This follows the dismissal of Yerbek Sagimbayev from the chairmanship. The committee had previously confirmed the detention of several individuals, including the heads of Samruk-Kazyna and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, on corruption charges.

item.title: US Treasury Chief Predicts Iran's Economy Could Shrink 25% by March 2027
item.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent predicts Iran's economy could contract by 25% by March 2027 due to U.S. pressure. He described the U.S. economic isolation campaign against Tehran as one of the most extensive in history, comparing its potential impact to the collapse of the Soviet Union's economy. The sanctions aim to cut off Iran's access to international financial networks and revenue generation.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Over 2.5 tons of crayfish seized in poaching bust
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Karaganda region have busted a group suspected of illegal crayfish fishing and sales. Authorities seized over 2.5 tons of crayfish, a truck, and a minivan from eight individuals. The estimated damage to the state is nearly 20 million tenge. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: 41 percent of villages in Kyrgyzstan have access to drinking water
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, 41 percent of villages are supplied with drinking water, according to the Deputy Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry. Out of 2,014 villages and 34 cities, 836 villages have access to potable water. Rehabilitation work is needed in 405 villages, while 773 are in the planning or construction stages.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Appoints New Head of Passenger Transport Division
item.description: Sultan Shabidinov has been appointed as the new chairman of the board for "Passenger Transport," a subsidiary of "Kazakhstan Temir Zholy" (KTZ). The decision was made by KTZ, the sole shareholder, on November 5, prior to the detention of KTZ head Yerzhan Otynshiyev on November 11.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Eldik Bank Unites International Climate Funds at COP31 Summit
item.description: Eldik Bank, a Kyrgyz financial institution, organized an international session at the UN Climate Summit COP31 in Antalya, bringing together leading global climate funds, development banks, and investment institutions. The event focused on attracting climate investments, expanding access to financing, and fostering partnerships.

item.title: SpaceX's Starship Completes Test Flight, Successfully Caught by Launch Tower
item.description: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft successfully returned to the launch pad and was caught by a specialized tower after a 22-hour test flight. This marks the first time a Starship vehicle has been successfully caught using this method, unlike previous landings which resulted in water landings or explosions.

item.title: Astana Company Faces Additional Tax Assessment of 4.7 Billion Tenge
item.description: A major company in Astana has been assessed an additional 4.7 billion tenge in taxes following a tax audit. The company had initially challenged the audit in court, but an appellate court overturned the lower court's decision, allowing the tax reassessment to stand. The supervisory body confirmed the additional tax amount.

item.title: Marat Irmenov Appointed Chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee
item.description: Marat Irmenov has been appointed as the new Chairman of the National Security Committee of Kazakhstan. This appointment marks a significant change in the leadership of the country's primary security agency.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Allocate 1.3 Trillion Tenge for "Children of Kazakhstan" Concept
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to spend 1.3 trillion tenge over five years on the "Children of Kazakhstan" concept, focusing on child safety, quality education, healthcare, and social protection. The plan includes 158 measures and 10 indicators, with many activities scheduled for 2026 and beyond. Several initiatives have already been completed ahead of schedule.

item.title: New Chairman Appointed to Kazakhstan's National Security Committee
item.description: Kazakhstan has a new head of the National Security Committee (KNB). Marat Irmenov was appointed by presidential decree, replacing Ermek Sagimbayev who had held the position since January 2022. Irmenov has served in national security agencies since 1996, previously holding leadership roles and serving as deputy chairman since October 2025.

item.title: Marat Irmenov appointed new chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Marat Irmenov as the new head of the National Security Committee (KNB) of Kazakhstan. Irmenov previously served as deputy chairman of the KNB and has a long career in national security agencies since 1996.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New National Security Committee Chairman
item.description: Ermek Sagimbayev has been dismissed as Chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee by presidential decree. Marat Irmenov has been appointed as his successor. Irmenov, a Major General of National Security, has a background in agriculture, law, and national security institutions.

item.title: Five EU Nations to Launch Rwanda Deportation Hub Scheme for Asylum Seekers
item.description: Five European Union countries are set to announce a plan to establish deportation hubs in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark, and the Netherlands aim to increase deportations and curb irregular migration, asserting compliance with international law.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dismisses National Security Committee Head
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan has dismissed Yermek Sagimbayev from his position as head of the National Security Committee (KNB). The specific reasons for the dismissal were not immediately disclosed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister Delivers 73 Ambulances to Ministry of Health
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers Chairman, Adylbek Kasymaliev, presented 73 new ambulances to the Ministry of Health. These vehicles, equipped with advanced medical equipment, will improve emergency medical services, especially in remote areas. The acquisition was part of a program supported by the World Bank.

item.title: Arrests of Fund Officials Raise Concerns Over Kazakhstan's Investment Climate
item.description: The detention of Nurlan Zhakupov, head of the Samruk-Kazyna sovereign wealth fund, and Yeldas Otinshev, head of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, on corruption charges could harm Kazakhstan's international reputation and investment attractiveness. Experts warn of questionable deals and macroeconomic risks following these high-profile arrests.

item.title: Pawnshop Network Suspected of Illegal Lending Operations in Astana
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated against a network of pawnshops in Astana for allegedly conducting illegal microfinance activities. The Financial Monitoring Agency claims the network issued loans under the guise of commission-based trade without a required license, with illicit profits exceeding 102 million tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Replaces Head of National Security Committee
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed Yermek Sagimbayev from his post as Chairman of Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB). Marat Irmenov has been appointed as the new chairman. Irmenov previously served as deputy chairman and has a background in national security operations and leadership roles.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Ranked Among World's 40 Most Influential Muslims
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev ranked 40th in The Muslim 500—2027 list of influential Muslims worldwide. The ranking highlighted reforms in Uzbekistan, including economic liberalization, improved foreign investment conditions, and eradication of forced labor in cotton. His foreign policy improvements and focus on Islamic heritage were also noted.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Block Online Games Violating Child Safety Requirements
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to legally mandate labeling and verification for online games, restricting access if violations are found. A draft law on digital and information security for children requires games to disclose potential risks like in-game purchases and user communication. An authorized state body will conduct checks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Six-Month Extension of Waste Paper Export Ban Outside EAEU
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy proposes extending the temporary ban on exporting waste paper, paper, and cardboard outside the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) for another six months. The ministry cites a shortage of secondary raw materials on the domestic market, which could impact production and jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet allocates 73 new ambulances to healthcare organizations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's First Deputy Prime Minister, Adylbek Kasymaliev, has instructed healthcare organizations to effectively utilize newly delivered ambulances and ensure their readiness for timely response to calls. He highlighted the link between public health, productivity, and technological development, noting a significant increase in healthcare funding.

item.title: Kazakhstan drafts new law to enhance digital and information security for children
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing a new law aimed at strengthening the protection of minors in the digital space. The bill includes requirements for labeling and describing digital products, including online games, detailing potential risks like in-game purchases and user communication. It also proposes mandatory checks and restrictions on non-compliant products.

item.title: Kazakhstan Refines Family Welfare Assessment to Include Debts and Housing Conditions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection has updated its methodology for assessing family welfare. The Digital Family Map now considers not only income and assets but also debts, housing quality, and family health. Certain income sources like state benefits and alimony are excluded from the calculation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Ombudsman for Protection of Scientists' Rights
item.description: Kazakhstan is introducing an ombudsman institution to protect the rights of scientists and researchers. The ombudsman will handle complaints, help resolve professional conflicts, and safeguard the interests of the scientific community. This follows legislative amendments in summer 2026, establishing the role within the National Academy of Sciences.

item.title: Five-Year-Old Sulaymon Battles Cancer, Needs Urgent Financial Support for Treatment
item.description: Five-year-old Sulaymon is fighting a high-risk, stage four neuroblastoma with bone marrow metastasis. He is undergoing treatment in Turkey, with several complex and expensive stages remaining. His family needs $380,000 to cover the costs of his ongoing medical care.

item.title: Osh Police Officer Forced to Kneel? Investigation Underway into Viral Video
item.description: A video circulating on social media shows a patrol police officer in Osh, Kyrgyzstan, kneeling and apologizing to an unidentified man. The circumstances are under investigation, with authorities examining the actions of both parties involved in the October 9th incident.

item.title: Iran Reportedly Threatens to Track Down Two US Navy Officers
item.description: Fox News reported that Iran has threatened to track down two US Navy officers, identified as the commanding and executive officers of the USS Spruance. This threat follows a warning from US President Donald Trump against assassinating American officials. Several US administration officials are reportedly being moved to secure residences due to security concerns.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Train 10 Million Youth in Future Professions by 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to train 10 million young people in digital skills and future professions by 2031, according to a presidential decree. The initiative aims to prepare specialists for the digital industry and modern labor market, with plans for regional programs, short-term courses in IT and AI, and a certification and voucher support system to promote employment.

item.title: Child Killed, Another Injured by Unexploded Ordnance in Afghanistan's Ghazni Province
item.description: A child has died and another was injured following the explosion of unexploded ordnance in Qarabagh District, Ghazni Province. The Taliban police command in Ghazni confirmed the incident occurred on Sunday. Afghanistan is among countries with high casualties from unexploded ordnance, with 64 incidents recorded in eastern Afghanistan since early 2026.
